# Feature: Mission — Composer & Live Run Screen

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-067
**Source Plan**: `.spec-lite/plan_ui.md`

Mission is the app's start page and the one place to start work. A user picks a mode (Ask, Research, Do, Run). They write a goal or pick a workflow, and they see the options that command actually honors. Each option shows its effective value and where that value came from (flag, environment variable name, preference key, or default). Submitting launches the run exactly once (D11) and opens the **cockpit**, a live run screen with these instruments:

- the top bar: Bindu, mode, goal echo, elapsed time, BudgetGauges and Stop;
- the **Understood** panel: contract summary, ContractRing and RequirementList;
- the **Engine** panel: RunTimeline;
- the **CliTwin**, which shows the exact `yantra` command and copies it for the user's shell.

The cockpit tells the truth about the run at all times. It shows the plan's explicit states, each with a next action:

- queued;
- starting;
- waiting for you;
- disconnected;
- worker not responding;
- engine stalled;
- needs review;
- start outcome unknown;
- live view unavailable.

It announces meaningful changes politely, never by stealing focus. A reload mid-run resumes with no gaps. When the run finishes, a View Transition morphs the cockpit into the run result.

From any finished run, a user can **Resume** when the core resumability rule allows it. They can also **Run again**, with current settings or the prior run's settings. Run again warns when the prior run may have had external effects.

Business value: this is the M2 milestone's visible half. A `research --no-llm` run starts, runs and finishes end to end in the app. It is also the path to the §14 success criterion that a non-terminal user completes a first `ask` within two minutes of `yantra ui`. CLI parity holds because the composer is generated from the FEAT-062 registry and every run shows its CLI twin.

### Acceptance (from plan §12)

- A `research --no-llm` run and a scripted fake-provider `do` run show every `RunEvent` in an instrument or in the EventInspector.
- The CLI twin, pasted into the default shell, starts the identical command.
- No inapplicable option appears.
- Stop is graceful. This is qualified by DEVIATION-1 below.
- A reload mid-run resumes with no gaps.
- Screen-reader output stays meaningful during a fast run.

### Deviations and clarifications (awaiting confirmation)

- **DEVIATION-1: Stop on `research`, `ask` and `run` is not graceful today.**
  - _Plan says:_ "Stop is graceful."
  - _What the code does:_ per `.spec-lite/TODO.md` ("Clean cancellation for `research`, `ask` and `run`", recorded during the FEAT-072 breakdown), only `do` and `doctor --agent-smoke` honor an abort signal. A Stop on the other run-class commands falls through to FEAT-064's forced termination, then reconciliation. The run ends `execution_state: interrupted` with `owner_lost`, not `aborted`.
  - _This feature:_ Stop is graceful wherever the handler honors abort. Everywhere else the cockpit says honestly, before and during the stop, that the command cannot stop cleanly and will be force-stopped after 10 s (TASK-008). The plan's "graceful Stop" acceptance is verified on `do`.
  - _What would close it:_ the existing TODO entry, which threads `context.signal` into the research loop, the ask pipeline and the replay orchestrator. That work is out of scope here.
- **DEVIATION-2: "Resumable" follows core's rule, not the plan's paraphrase.**
  - _Plan says (§8 Reliability matrix):_ resumable means "checkpoint exists, failure class permits".
  - _What core does:_ `packages/core/src/workflow/replay/resume.ts` resumes a **workflow** run when all of these hold:
    - the manifest status is `failed` or `paused`;
    - the profile is not ephemeral;
    - `plan.json` is readable.
  - A missing checkpoint resumes from step 0. Failure classes `scope_violation` and `ethics_refused` do not forbid resume; they **require consent** (`--force`).
  - Agentic `ask`/`research`/`do` runs are never resumable; `yantra resume` takes workflow runs only.
  - _This feature:_ the app follows core's rule through a single non-throwing predicate that `loadResumePoint` also uses (TASK-013), so the rule cannot diverge. A consent-required class shows Resume behind an explicit acknowledgement that adds `--force`.

## 2. Data Model (Granular)

> `.spec-lite/data_model.md` does not exist. This feature adds **no persisted storage**. Everything here is an in-memory client model, a protocol read schema, or a pure core result type. Persisted run state (`run-events.jsonl`, `execution-receipt.json`, invocation records, leases) is owned by FEAT-063, FEAT-064, FEAT-065 and FEAT-072. This feature only reads it.

### Entities & Attributes

- **`CockpitState`** (apps/web, in-memory; produced by the pure reducer `reduceRunEvent`):
  - `runId` (string): the run being followed. NOT NULL.
  - `lastSeq` (number): the highest `seq` applied. Starts at -1. This is the dedupe and resubscribe cursor.
  - `mode` (`ask | research | do | run | resume | other`): from the invocation path or receipt.
  - `goal` (string | null): from the `goal_echo` event. Control characters are stripped and the length is capped at 200, mirroring `GOAL_ECHO_MAX_CHARS`.
  - `startedAt` (ISO string | null): from the first `task_started` or receipt event.
  - `contract` (`{revision: number, summary: string}` | null): from the latest `contract_declared`.
  - `requirements` (readonly `LiveRequirement[]`): from the latest `progress.items`. Each item is `{id, kind: fill|artifact|effects|deliverable, label, state: pending|advancing|met, done, total}`.
  - `capabilityGaps` (readonly `{item, summary}[]`): from `capability_gap`.
  - `budgets` (`BudgetView` | null): from the latest `budget_snapshot`.
  - `timeline` (`TimelineWindow`): a bounded ring buffer of the newest 2,000 timeline entries plus a total count. Older entries remain readable from the run result's JSONL viewer (FEAT-066).
  - `engine` (`idle | thinking | acting | stalled`): derived from the tool lifecycle and `recovery` events.
  - `pendingInterventions` (readonly `{interventionId, kind, summary, deadlineAt}[]`): from `intervention_raised` minus `intervention_resolved`.
  - `outcome` (`{outcome, terminationReason, executionState?}` | null): from `run_outcome`.
  - `inspected` (`InspectorWindow`): a bounded window of events routed to the EventInspector, including unknown kinds.
  - `phase` (string | null): the latest deterministic `ask`/`research` phase (search, fetch, extract, synthesize).
- **`DisplayedState`** (apps/web; produced by the pure `deriveDisplayedState`):
  - `kind`: one of the following.

    ```text
    queued | starting | running | waiting_for_you | disconnected | worker_not_responding
    | engine_stalled | needs_review | start_unknown | live_view_unavailable | stopping
    | finished
    ```

  - `detail` (string): the plain-language line, using CLI words verbatim.
  - `position` (number | null): the queue position when `queued`.
  - `nextActions` (readonly `NextAction[]`): `{id, label, invocation?: CommandInvocation, rpc?: string}`. Every action names an engineered path (memory → Coding Standards, advice rule).
  - Precedence when several conditions hold, highest first:

    ```text
    disconnected > live_view_unavailable > worker_not_responding > needs_review > start_unknown
    > waiting_for_you > stopping > engine_stalled > finished > running > starting > queued
    ```

- **`ComposerModel`** (apps/web; produced by `buildComposerModel(registry, commandPath, argv, effective)`):
  - `commandPath` (readonly string[]): `['ask']`, `['research']`, `['do']`, `['run']` or `['resume']`.
  - `positional` (`{name, inputKind, value, required}`): goal, topic, query or workflow name.
  - `fields` (readonly `ComposerField[]`). Each field is `{optionName, flag, inputKind, label, help, value, effective: EffectiveOptionView, relations, danger, disabledReason?}`. Only options that are applicable for this command **and** surfaced in the app appear.
  - `workflowParams` (readonly `{key, type, required, value}[]`): Run mode only, from the selected workflow's declared params. Serialized as repeated `--params key=value`.
  - `errors` (readonly `{field, message}[]`): relation violations (`requires`, `conflicts`) and input-kind validation.
- **`EffectiveOptionView`** (protocol read schema `EffectiveOptions`, served by the host):
  - `option` (string): the registry option name.
  - `value` (JSON value | null): the effective value. **Never a secret value.** A secret-reference option shows the reference name only.
  - `source`: `{kind: 'flag'} | {kind: 'env', name} | {kind: 'preference', key} | {kind: 'default'}`. This is the FEAT-072 settings-resolver source vocabulary, so it matches what the receipt records.
- **`ProviderReadiness`** (protocol read schema): `{ready: boolean, provider: string, model: string, reason?: string, fix?: {label, invocation: CommandInvocation}}`.
- **`RunRecoveryAssessment`** (protocol read schema; core pure result types):
  - `resume`: one of
    - `{available: false, reason}`;
    - `{available: true, requiresConsent: boolean, failureClass?}`.
  - `runAgain`:
    - `{prior: 'receipt' | 'reconstructed' | 'goal_only', invocation: CommandInvocation | null}`;
    - `effects: 'none' | 'possible' | 'verified'`;
    - `effectReasons: readonly string[]`.

    Effect reasons are drawn from:
    - verified `fill`/`click` actions in the Brief's `actions`;
    - a contract with `effects.submit: allowed`;
    - workflow steps that submit;
    - legacy runs of an `external`-effect command with no evidence, which yield `possible`.

### Relationships

- One `CockpitState` follows one run (`runId`). A run is reached either through an invocation (`invocation_id` → `run_id` from FEAT-065's invocation record) or directly by run ID.
- `ComposerModel` 1:1 a registry command entry (FEAT-062). Each `ComposerField` maps 1:1 to a registry option and 1:1 to an `EffectiveOptionView` row.
- `RunRecoveryAssessment` 1:1 a finished run directory. It is derived from the manifest, `execution-receipt.json` (or the manifest, for reconstruction), the Brief, and the contract.

### Indexes & Constraints

- **Seq dedupe:**
  - the reducer ignores any event with `seq <= lastSeq`;
  - a gap (`seq > lastSeq + 1`) is never applied out of order. The stream resubscribes from `lastSeq + 1`.
- **Bounded memory:**
  - the timeline and inspector windows are capped;
  - reducer cost is O(1) per event, with no full-state copy per event, so a 50,000-event replay stays responsive.
- **Invocation IDs** are client-generated (`crypto.randomUUID()`) once per submission. The ID is reused on every retry of the same submission (D11 idempotency).
- **The composer never places a secret value in argv.** An option of input kind `secret-input` is not rendered. The composer links to Credentials (FEAT-071) instead.

- **FEAT-062 (Command Registry):**

  - the settings resolver, which the effective-options read reuses read-only so the grammar is not duplicated (memory → Coding Standards);

  - `research` and `do` running under the worker adapter;
  - the per-command `honorsAbort` fact.
- **FEAT-063 (Run-Event Stream):** the `RunEvent` union with `seq`, `goal_echo`, `budget_snapshot`, `contract_declared`, `progress`, `recovery`, phase events, `intervention_*` and `run_outcome`.
- **FEAT-064 (Ownership & Channel):** run socket `cancel`, heartbeat, handshake (D17), and forced termination followed by reconciliation.
- **FEAT-065 (App Host):**
  - the RPC (`command.invoke`, `command.cancel`, `queue.*`, `run.subscribe`, `read.*`);
  - invocation records and states;
  - session info, including host platform for the default twin shell;
  - the app shell, top bar and Bindu slot.
- **FEAT-066 (Run Results & Audit):**
  - the `/runs/<id>` route (View Transition target);
  - RequirementList, OutcomeBadge and EventInspector instruments;
  - the artifact viewers.
- **Interventions:** FEAT-068 renders and answers interventions (GuardedSwitch, Inbox).
  - **STUB:** Until FEAT-068 lands, _waiting for you_ shows the intervention summary and deadline. Its next action is "Answer in the terminal" with the `yantra confirm <run-id> grant|deny` CLI twin. FEAT-068 replaces it with the in-app GuardedSwitch.
- **Live browser view:** FEAT-069 replaces the neutral backdrop with the live browser view. This feature leaves a `backdrop` slot in the cockpit layout.

## 5. Implementation Tasks

Task order follows plan §8. TASK-001 to TASK-008 are the **M2 cockpit subset**, enough for a `research --no-llm` run end to end. TASK-009 to TASK-016 complete the feature.

### TASK-001: Follow a run's event stream with gap-free, duplicate-free replay and reconnect

- [ ] **Implementation:**
  - **Pure reducer.** Create `apps/web/src/live/cockpit-state.ts` with `initialCockpitState(runId)` and the pure `reduceRunEvent(state, {seq, event})`, implementing the §2 fields.
    - Seq rule: an event with `seq <= lastSeq` is a no-op. An event with `seq > lastSeq + 1` is not applied; it returns `{state, gap: true}`.
    - Timeline and inspector are bounded ring windows.
  - **Run stream store.** Create `apps/web/src/live/run-stream.ts` with `createRunStream({rpc, runId, clock})`, an external store with `subscribe`/`getSnapshot`.
    - It calls `run.subscribe {run_id, from_seq: lastSeq + 1}`.
    - On a gap or a socket reconnect, it resubscribes from `lastSeq + 1`.
    - It batches applied events per animation frame, so a replay of thousands of events renders once per frame.
  - **Hooks.** Create `use-run-stream.ts` with `useRunStream(runId)` and selector hooks over `useSyncExternalStore`. There are no global singletons: the store is created per route, and the RPC client is injected through context.
- [ ] **Unit Tests:** `apps/web/tests/live/cockpit-state.spec.ts` and `run-stream.spec.ts`:
  - a duplicate seq is ignored;
  - a gap triggers resubscribe from `lastSeq + 1`, and the final state equals a straight replay;
  - reconnect mid-stream yields no duplicate timeline entries;
  - replay of 50,000 synthetic events completes under a fixed budget, with the timeline capped at 2,000 and the total count correct;
  - a `progress` event replaces requirements wholesale;
  - `intervention_resolved` removes its pending item;
  - `run_outcome` sets the outcome, including `execution_state: interrupted` with `owner_lost`;
  - batching uses a stepped fake clock, never wall time (memory → Testing).
- [ ] **Documentation Update:** Invoke **Document** update mode for the Yantra app → Mission (live run stream and reload behavior).
- **Verify:** `cd apps/web && npx vitest run tests/live` passes. Stopping and restarting a fake RPC mid-stream in the test yields a state deep-equal to an uninterrupted replay.

### TASK-005: Explicit run states with next actions (queued through live view unavailable)

- [ ] **Implementation:**
  - **Pure derivation.** Create `apps/web/src/live/displayed-state.ts` with the pure `deriveDisplayedState({invocation, connection, channel, cockpit, stopping})`. It implements every §8 displayed state with §2 precedence:

    | Displayed state         | Derived from                                                             | Next actions                                                                                                                                   |
    | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
    | `queued`                | invocation `queued`, with its position                                   | Cancel (`command.cancel`)                                                                                                                      |
    | `starting`              | `reserved`, `spawning` or `claimed` with no event yet                    | —                                                                                                                                              |
    | `needs_review`          | `needs_review`                                                           | the three D13 choices (`queue.resolve_review {choice}`)                                                                                        |
    | `start_unknown`         | `start_unknown`                                                          | Start anyway, with a possible-duplicate-effects warning (`queue.start` with explicit confirmation); Discard                                    |
    | `waiting_for_you`       | a pending intervention                                                   | the FEAT-068 STUB action (§4)                                                                                                                  |
    | `disconnected`          | the app's WebSocket to the host is down                                  | Retry now; the store keeps reconnecting with backoff                                                                                           |
    | `worker_not_responding` | `run.channel_status = not_responding`                                    | Stop                                                                                                                                           |
    | `live_view_unavailable` | `run.channel_status = unavailable`                                       | Open the run result; the D17 message, "Started by Yantra <version>; live view unavailable. The run continues and its result will appear here." |
    | `engine_stalled`        | the latest `recovery` event has `trigger: stalled` and no newer progress | Keep waiting; Stop                                                                                                                             |
    | `finished`              | a `run_outcome`                                                          | Open the result                                                                                                                                |

  - **Status banner.** Create `packages/ui/src/instruments/run-status-banner.tsx`, which renders the state word, the detail and next-action buttons.

  - **Invocation route.** Create `apps/web/src/routes/mission/invocations.$invocationId.tsx`. It follows the invocation and redirects with `replace` to `runs.$runId` once a run ID exists.

## 6. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth:**
  - All reads and RPCs go through FEAT-065's authenticated WebSocket, with a per-window capability. This feature adds reads only behind that session.
  - Answers to interventions are FEAT-068's. The cockpit never stamps `user_app`.
  - Credential values never pass through the composer. `secret-input` options are not rendered, and secret-reference options carry names only (plan §7).
- **Error Handling:**
  - Host reads return typed RPC errors with safe messages and, where one exists, a remediation naming a real command (memory → Coding Standards).
  - Corrupt or missing run artifacts degrade per item, as in `prior-invocation` and `prior-effects`, never per page.
  - Rejected invocations show the host's `{exit_code, code, message, remediation}` inline.
  - `busy` (exit 3) from locked resources is shown with the holder's description.
  - A disconnected socket is a displayed state, not an error toast.
- **Logging:**
  - The app does not log to the console in production.
  - The host logs new reads only on failure: read name and error code, never argv values, effective values, goals or secrets (plan §11).
  - Channel-status changes are logged once per change by the host, never per heartbeat.
  - Announcements and copied commands are not logged.
- **Security:**
  - Goal echo, contract summaries, tool summaries and URLs are untrusted page- or model-derived text. They render through React escaping only, with no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`.
  - External links carry `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.
  - The outbound canary scan (FEAT-065 suite) covers the new read responses.
- **Accessibility:**
  - Status never relies on color alone.
  - There is one polite live region, and focus moves only on user action.
  - All controls are Drshya primitives on React Aria.
  - Reduced motion and Solid mode are honored.
- **Design system:**
  - Only Drshya semantic utilities; no raw palette utilities, hex or `oklch()` literals.
  - Icons only from the semantic registry.
  - CLI words are rendered verbatim from protocol values (plan §9).
